When sync env vars are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches callers to this schema; the Salesforce CalendarService diff shows a refresh against login.salesforce.com (unconditional of sync) whose parsed key is persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } } })`, so instance_url and signature would be stripped from stored credentials, and O365's expiry_date would never be set, forcing a refresh + DB write on every operation. judged_text: The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (duplicate key, second wins), so minimumTokenResponseSchema is really {access_token: string} and zod's default unknown-key stripping deletes every other field of the response — it does not 'assume any property with a number is the expiry' as the comments claim. Once the sync env vars are set, every parseRefreshTokenResponse caller silently switches to this schema: Salesforce (which refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com regardless of sync) persists a key of only {access_token, refresh_token}, stripping instance_url from a response that contained it, so the next jsforce.Connection is built with instanceUrl undefined and all Salesforce calls fail; Office365 never receives a new expiry, so it re-refreshes (sync-endpoint POST plus a credential DB write) on every operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate to a single literal string key at runtime (commonly `"[object Object]"`), so this does not match “any numeric property” as the comment claims. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, when the min schema path is activated (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` && `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), most token response fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc.) will be dropped. This can directly break integrations relying on those fields (e.g., Office365 expiry handling; Salesforce persisting refreshed tokens without `instance_url`), matching the finding’s core claim about schema behavior and resulting data loss.
